name: Glipizide
mechanism: Stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells
dosing: Start 2.5–5 mg orally before breakfast, increase gradually depending on glycaemic response; usual maximum 20 mg daily (may divide doses); use with caution in elderly and those with renal impairment
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes, diabetic ketoacidosis, known hypersensitivity to sulfonylureas; caution in severe hepatic impairment
interactions: Drugs that increase hypoglycaemia risk (e.g., other antidiabetics, sulfonamides) or reduce efficacy (e.g., corticosteroids); rifampicin and other enzyme inducers may reduce effect
monitoring: Regular blood glucose monitoring during initiation and dose changes; assess HbA1c periodically; monitor for symptoms of hypoglycaemia especially in elderly or patients with renal impairment
pregnancy: Avoid - insulin is preferred for glycaemic control in pregnancy
sideEffects: Hypoglycaemia (major risk), weight gain, gastrointestinal upset, rash; hypoglycaemia risk increased in elderly and those with renal impairment
pharmacokinetics: Oral administration; shorter-acting sulfonylurea with hepatic metabolism and renal excretion of metabolites
clinicalPearls: Shorter-acting agent among sulfonylureas; consider alternatives (e.g., gliclazide or insulin) in frail/elderly to reduce prolonged hypoglycaemia risk; adjust dose with renal impairment
indication: Type 2 diabetes mellitus for additional glycaemic control when diet, exercise and metformin (or other first-line therapy) are insufficient
